extra.message: Every query-string parameter prefixed 'R_' (RunreportsApiResource.getReportParams, lines 160-175) is taken verbatim and substituted via naive string replace (genericDataService.replace) into the stored 'stretchy report' SQL template, with no escaping or bind parameters, before execution via jdbcTemplate.queryForRowSet. Any report parameter value can inject arbitrary SQL.

getSql() builds a SQL string with 'name' (the raw {reportName} path param from GET /runreports/{reportName}, only checked against a permission table, never escaped) concatenated directly into a quoted string literal, enabling SQL injection via a crafted report name.

The 'order' query param from GET /datatables/{datatable}/{apptableId} (DatatablesApiResource.java:170-175) is concatenated unescaped into an ORDER BY clause with no allow-listing, enabling SQL injection via subquery/boolean constructs in ORDER BY.

'datatable'/'dataTableName', the raw {datatable}/{surveyName} path segment from the datatables and survey APIs, is never regex-validated on CRUD-entry/GET endpoints (only on admin create/alter/delete-table endpoints) and is concatenated directly into a quoted SQL string literal here, allowing injection via a single quote in the path segment.

Unvalidated 'datatable' path parameter flows via createDatatableEntry -> CommandWrapperBuilder -> CreateDatatableEntryCommandHandler into getAddSql, which concatenates it directly as a backtick-quoted table/column identifier in an INSERT statement executed via jdbcTemplate.update(sql), allowing identifier-based SQL injection.

The same unvalidated 'datatable' path parameter reaches an UPDATE statement via updateDatatableEntryOneToOne/OneToMany -> getUpdateSql; column values are escaped but the table name itself is concatenated unescaped as a SQL identifier.
deleteDatatableEntries/deleteDatatableEntry build a DELETE statement by concatenating the unvalidated 'datatable' path parameter directly as a backtick-quoted table name.

'surveyName', the raw {surveyName} path param from GET /survey/{surveyName} (SurveyApiResource.retrieveSurvey), is concatenated unescaped into a quoted SQL literal with no validation, enabling SQL injection.

The 'sqlSearch' query param from GET /staff (StaffApiResource.java:88-104) is appended verbatim as a WHERE-clause fragment at line 224 ('extraCriteria.append(" and (").append(sqlSearch).append(")")') with no bind parameters or escaping, then executed via jdbcTemplate.query, enabling arbitrary boolean/UNION-based SQL injection.

'orderBy' (line 163: 'sqlBuilder.append(" order by ").append(searchParameters.getOrderBy())') and 'sqlSearch' (line 198: 'extraCriteria = " and (" + sqlSearch + ")"'), both raw query params on GET /clients (ClientsApiResource.java:125-147), are concatenated directly into SQL with no allow-list/escaping, unlike sibling search fields that use ApiParameterHelper.sqlEncodeString.

'sqlSearch' from GET /groups (GroupsApiResource.java:168-182) is appended unescaped as a WHERE-clause fragment ('extraCriteria.append(" and ( ").append(sqlSearch).append(") ")'); 'orderBy'/'sortOrder' are similarly concatenated unescaped at line 158, enabling SQL injection.

'sqlSearch' from GET /centers (CentersApiResource.java:142-166) is appended unescaped as a WHERE-clause fragment ('extraCriteria.append(" and (").append(sqlQueryCriteria).append(") ")'); 'orderBy'/'sortOrder' are similarly concatenated unescaped at lines 349 and 384, enabling SQL injection.

'sqlSearch' and 'orderBy' from GET /savingsaccounts (SavingsAccountsApiResource.java:112-120) are concatenated unescaped into the WHERE and ORDER BY clauses ('sqlBuilder.append(" and (").append(sqlQueryCriteria).append(")")' and 'sqlBuilder.append(" order by ").append(searchParameters.getOrderBy())'), reaching jdbcTemplate via paginationHelper.fetchPage, enabling SQL injection.

'sqlSearch' and 'orderBy' from GET /loans (LoansApiResource.java:576-585) are concatenated unescaped into the WHERE and ORDER BY clauses, reaching jdbcTemplate with no bind parameters, enabling SQL injection.

'orderBy' from GET /accounttransfers (AccountTransfersApiResource.java:106-115) is concatenated unescaped into an ORDER BY clause ('sqlBuilder.append(" order by ").append(searchParameters.getOrderBy())') with no allow-list of sortable columns, enabling SQL injection.
Second occurrence of the same unescaped ORDER BY concatenation of the 'orderBy' request parameter.

'orderBy'/'sortOrder' from GET /standinginstructions (StandingInstructionApiResource.java:149-184) are concatenated unescaped into the ORDER BY clause with no allow-list of sortable columns, enabling SQL injection.

The client-supplied multipart filename (fileDetails.getFileName(), DocumentManagementApiResource.java:118,150) is validated only for non-blank/length by DocumentCommandValidator, then concatenated with File.separator onto the upload directory and written to disk, allowing a '../'-laden filename to write outside the per-entity document directory.

The client-supplied multipart filename (fileDetails.getFileName(), ImagesApiResource.java:90,94) is checked only for non-emptiness/MIME type, never for '../' sequences, before being concatenated into the on-disk image path and written, allowing path traversal.

'reportName', the raw {reportName} URL path segment (RunreportsApiResource.java:80,105), is checked only against a permission table (never canonicalized or filtered for '../') before being concatenated directly into the PDF output filesystem path and used in a FileOutputStream, letting an authenticated reporting user write the generated file to an arbitrary location.

'mappingString' comes verbatim from the 'config' JSON field accepted by MixTaxonomyMappingApiResource.updateTaxonomyMapping (PUT /mixmapping) and is stored unvalidated; only '{glcode}' placeholders are substituted before the full string is executed by the Nashorn ScriptEngine.eval, giving arbitrary code execution (including Java interop, e.g. java.lang.Runtime) to any user able to update the taxonomy mapping.

mergeTemplate merges an arbitrary attacker-controlled JSON body and query params (including an attacker-controlled 'BASE_URI' override) into a stored Mustache template scope with no permission check (unlike sibling endpoints in the same class), then compiles/executes mapper URLs built from that scope server-side.

A URL built from attacker-influenced Mustache scope data is fetched via HttpURLConnection.openConnection() with no destination allow-list. The currently authenticated user's real credentials (read from SecurityContextHolder) or a stored auth token are attached as Basic Auth to the outbound request, so the SSRF also forwards live session credentials to an arbitrary attacker-controlled host.

Every outbound mapper-URL fetch calls TrustModifier.relaxHostChecking(connection), disabling TLS certificate and hostname validation, so the SSRF above can also be used to MITM the proxied credentials/response over 'HTTPS'.

The hostname verifier unconditionally returns true and the trust manager's checkServerTrusted is a no-op, accepting any certificate for any host. This is wired into the production TemplateMergeService.getConnection path reachable from the public mergeTemplate API, not test-only code.

Creating/updating a hook makes the server issue a live HTTP request to the user-supplied 'Payload URL' as a validity check, with no scheme/host allow-list (e.g. can target 169.254.169.254 or internal services) — SSRF triggered purely by hook configuration, before any event ever fires.
On every webhook event, the server POSTs the event payload to a user-configured 'Payload URL' hook field with no validation that it isn't an internal/loopback/link-local address.
The user-configured SMS-bridge URL hook field is used directly to build and issue the outbound HTTP request with no host/scheme allow-list, allowing SSRF.

createClient()/createWebHookService() build the OkHttpClient used for all webhook/SMS-bridge deliveries with certificate validation and hostname verification fully disabled ('public boolean verify(...) { return true; }' and a no-op checkServerTrusted), compounding the webhook SSRF findings with MITM risk.
'reportName', a raw path parameter, is only space-stripped (not CRLF/quote-sanitized) before being placed into the Content-Disposition header value on CSV export.
'entityDisplayName', a user-editable client/staff display name field, is reflected unsanitized into the Content-Disposition header on image download.
The stored document filename, attacker-chosen at upload time, is reflected unsanitized into the Content-Disposition header on download.

The raw 'oauth_token' request parameter is concatenated unencoded into the redirect target used for the Location header on authentication failure; the base URL is fixed, but the parameter itself is not URL/header-encoded, risking CRLF/header injection depending on servlet-container strictness.

CORS is wildcard-open ('Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *') on every API response, and 'Access-Control-Allow-Headers' echoes back whatever the client requests. Duplicated in TenantAwareTenantIdentifierFilter.java:100-105. No Allow-Credentials:true was found alongside it, which caps impact, but unrestricted origin on a financial API is an avoidable misconfiguration.

Arbitrary attacker-controlled JSON body keys/values and query params are merged into a server-stored Mustache template and returned with Content-Type text/html, with no permission check. Mustache escapes '{{var}}' but not '{{{var}}}'; any template using triple-mustache fields reflects unescaped attacker input as HTML/JS.

Password is accepted as a URL query parameter ('@QueryParam("password")') on the authenticate endpoint; it is recorded in server access logs, proxy/load-balancer logs, browser history, and Referer headers.
Same query-string password exposure as the main authentication endpoint, duplicated for the self-service API.

On deadlock/optimistic-lock retry, the full raw request JSON (command.json()) is logged — including plaintext passwords for user-create/update and password-reset commands — writing credentials unredacted into application logs.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: For any unrecognized RuntimeException (and Spring TransactionException) raised inside a Batch API sub-request, the raw exception message/toString() — including exception class name and underlying DB/driver error text — is embedded directly into the JSON response returned to the client instead of a sanitized message.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: Passing limit=0 or a negative value on any paginated listing endpoint disables the cap entirely ('checkedLimit = null'), so isLimited() becomes false and no SQL LIMIT clause is appended (e.g. ClientReadPlatformServiceImpl.java:170-171), allowing a single request to force a full unbounded table scan/result set.

Unlike the multipart upload path which validates file size, the base64 Data-URL image upload path (ImagesApiResource.addNewClientImage, lines 102-113) performs no size check before decoding and writing to disk, letting a client submit an arbitrarily large request body to exhaust memory/disk.

createDocument/updateDocument/deleteDocument call documentWritePlatformService directly with no validateHasReadPermission/validateHasWritePermission check and are not routed through the command-wrapper pattern. Any authenticated user can upload, overwrite, or delete a document (identity documents, contracts, etc.) on any entity.

updateDocument/deleteDocument fetch a Document purely by documentId without verifying it belongs to the entityType/entityId in the URL or to the caller's office hierarchy (code even has TODO comments at lines 98-100 and 139 acknowledging the missing check). Any authenticated user can update/delete any document by guessing/incrementing documentId.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: Document listing/retrieval/download is gated only by a single generic DOCUMENT permission with no entity-type-specific check and no office-hierarchy restriction in the SQL (TODO comment at line ~60 acknowledges this), so any user holding that one permission can view/download documents for any entity across any office of the tenant.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: addNewClientImage/updateClientImage/deleteClientImage call imageWritePlatformService.saveOrUpdateImage/deleteImage after only validating the entity type — no validateHasReadPermission('CLIENTIMAGE'/'STAFFIMAGE') like the sibling GET methods have, and ImageWritePlatformServiceJpaRepositoryImpl has no PlatformSecurityContext at all. Any authenticated user can upload, replace, or delete any client's or staff member's photo.

retrieveCommands and retrieveAuditSearchTemplate call readPlatformService directly with no validateHasReadPermission check, unlike the sibling AuditsApiResource which checks 'AUDIT' permission for the equivalent endpoints. Any authenticated user can list every pending maker-checker entry tenant-wide, including full command JSON (e.g. plaintext passwords in not-yet-approved user-creation commands), bypassing the two-person-control confidentiality the feature is meant to provide.

The injected securityContext field is never used in any of the read methods (getTellerData, findTeller, getCashierData, getTransactionsForCashier, getJournalData, etc.). Every read endpoint for teller/cashier cash management is reachable by any authenticated user with no TELLER permission check and no office scoping.

getCashierData calls readPlatformService.getCashierData directly; the class does not even inject PlatformSecurityContext. Cashier cash-drawer data for any office/teller/staff is retrievable by any authenticated user with no permission check whatsoever.

getJournalData calls readPlatformService.getJournals directly; the injected securityContext field is unused. Teller cash-journal entries across any office/teller/cashier are exposed to any authenticated user with no authorization check.

findBySurvey/findBySurveyClient call only securityContext.authenticatedUser() with no validateHasReadPermission, and clientRepository.findOne(clientId) is used with no office-hierarchy check. Any authenticated user can retrieve any client's survey/credit-scorecard answers tenant-wide via the clientId path parameter.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: getResourceCondition builds SQL filtered only by client_id/loan_id/group_id etc. with no join on m_office/hierarchy (unlike ClientIdentifierReadPlatformServiceImpl which filters with 'o.hierarchy like ?'). Because NotesApiResource gates notes only by a generic role permission, a staff member with that permission in one branch can read notes belonging to clients/loans in any other branch by varying the resourceId path parameter.
